# cachekit (@mohamedhabibwork/cachekit)

> Provider-first, runtime-portable TypeScript caching for Node.js >= 20, Bun, and Deno. One deliberate cache contract — TTL, stale-while-revalidate, tag invalidation, deduplicated `getOrSet`, codecs — with a full in-memory provider that needs zero dependencies and a Redis-protocol provider whose optional `redis` peer is loaded only when you create it (or inject your own client). Dual ESM/CJS with full TypeScript declarations.

## Install

```bash
npm install @mohamedhabibwork/cachekit
# The Redis-protocol provider is the only place an SDK is ever needed:
npm install @mohamedhabibwork/cachekit redis
# …or inject your own compatible client and install nothing extra.
```

**Entrypoints** (import only what you use): `@mohamedhabibwork/cachekit`
(core + memory + factory), `.../memory`, `.../redis`, `.../valkey`,
`.../dragonfly`, `.../elasticache`, `.../memorystore`, `.../azure-redis`
(Redis-protocol services), `.../testing` (fake clock + fake cache).

If `redis` is missing when a connection must be auto-created, the provider
throws `CacheDependencyMissingError` with the exact `npm install` command —
never a module-not-found crash.

## Quick start

```ts
import { createCache } from "@mohamedhabibwork/cachekit";

const cache = await createCache({ type: "memory", namespace: "catalog:v1", defaultTtl: "5m" });

await cache.set("product:42", { id: 42, name: "Keyboard" }, { ttl: "5m", tags: ["products"] });

const product = await cache.get<{ id: number }>("product:42"); // fresh-only by default

const loaded = await cache.getOrSet("product:43", async () => fetchFromDb(43), {
  ttl: "10m",
  staleTtl: "1h",      // serve stale while one caller refreshes
});
```

## Core API

```ts
cache.get<V>(key, { allowStale?: boolean, signal? });         // miss => undefined; null is cacheable
cache.getMany<V>(keys, options?);
cache.set(key, value, { ttl?, staleTtl?, tags?, native?, overwrite?, signal? });
cache.getOrSet<V>(key, loader: ({ signal }) => V | Promise<V>, { ttl?, staleTtl?, serveStale?, tags? });
cache.delete(key, options?);
cache.deleteMany(keys, options?);
cache.invalidateTags(tags, options?);                          // TagInvalidationResult
cache.clear(options?);
cache.health?();                                              // provider health, where supported
await cache.close();
cache.capabilities;                                           // { ttl, atomicSetIfAbsent, tags, getMany, clearNamespace, distributedLocks, pubsubInvalidation, persistence }
```

## Manager (named caches)

Lazy per-name creation from config, warmup, per-cache health, single close.

```ts
import { createCacheManager } from "@mohamedhabibwork/cachekit";
const caches = createCacheManager({
  default: "catalog",
  caches: {
    catalog: { type: "memory", namespace: "catalog:v1", defaultTtl: "5m" },
    sessions: { type: "redis", url: process.env.REDIS_URL },
  },
});
const catalog = await caches.cache("catalog"); // Promise<Cache<"memory">>, instance reused
await caches.default();          // the default cache
await caches.warmup();           // create all configured caches now (fails fast on bad config)
await caches.health();           // Record<name, CacheHealth { status: ok|degraded|error, provider, latency, details? }>
await caches.close();            // close every created cache, forget instances
```
Unknown names reject with CacheInvalidConfigError; failed creations are evicted so the next call retries.

## Helpers

- `increment(cache, key, { by?, ttl?, clock? })` / `decrement(...)`: locked read-modify-write counter; TTL set only on creation (fixed window).
- `addIfAbsent(cache, key, value, setOptions)` -> boolean; `pull(cache, key)` reads then deletes.
- `memoize(cache, fn, { key: (...args) => key, tags?: (...args) => string[], ttl? })` wraps fn with getOrSet.
- `namespaced(cache, prefix)`: scoped view storing `prefix:key`; tags global; clear() throws; close() no-op.
- `createLayeredCache({ l1, l2, l1Ttl?, closeLayers? })`: read L1 then L2 with backfill; writes/deletes/tags hit both; locks + capabilities from L2.
- Memory `maxEntries` evicts least-recently-used. Full examples: docs/use-cases.md.

## Semantics (do not get these wrong)

- A cache miss is `undefined`; `null` is a cacheable value.
- `ttl` is the fresh period; `staleTtl` adds a stale window. `get()` returns
  fresh values only — pass `allowStale: true` to accept in-window stale data.
- `getOrSet()` deduplicates concurrent loads in-process. With a stale entry it
  returns stale immediately while one caller refreshes, unless `serveStale: false`.
- Built-in codecs: `json` (default), `text`, `bytes`. Custom codecs need
  `name`, `encode`, `decode`.
- Keys and tags reject control characters; namespaces use an internal separator.
- Inspect `capabilities` before relying on provider-specific behavior —
  unsupported operations throw `CacheUnsupportedOperationError`, they are never
  silently emulated.

## Providers

| Provider        | Entrypoint  | Extra dependency                                   |
| --------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Memory          | root `/memory` | none — TTL, SWR, tags, locks, codecs            |
| Redis protocol  | `/redis`    | optional `redis` peer; inject a client instead     |
| Valkey          | `/valkey`   | same as redis                                      |
| Dragonfly       | `/dragonfly`| same as redis                                      |
| ElastiCache     | `/elasticache` | same as redis                                   |
| Memorystore     | `/memorystore` | same as redis                                   |
| Azure Cache for Redis | `/azure-redis` | same as redis                            |
| Custom          | root        | register with `defineCacheProvider` / `registerCacheProvider` |

Redis-protocol providers work against any compatible endpoint (Redis, Valkey,
ElastiCache, Memorystore, Dragonfly). Tags and namespace clear are
deliberately `unsupported` there (inspect `capabilities`); distributed locks
are native.

## Errors

`CacheError` base; subclasses: `CacheInvalidConfigError`,
`CacheDependencyMissingError` (missing optional SDK — message contains the
install command), `CacheDecodeError`, `CacheSerializationError`,
`CacheLockTimeoutError`, `CacheUnsupportedOperationError`, `CacheClosedError`.
Everything network-bound accepts `signal`.

## Testing

```ts
import { createMemoryCache } from "@mohamedhabibwork/cachekit";
import { createFakeClock } from "@mohamedhabibwork/cachekit/testing";
const clock = createFakeClock();
const cache = await createMemoryCache({ clock: clock.now }); // deterministic TTL tests
clock.advance(60_000); // time travel
```

## Runtime support

- Node.js >= 20 (primary), Bun, Deno. Dual ESM/CJS with full declarations.
- Core has no runtime dependencies at all.
